Cinnamon Churros

Served at: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Serves 8Prep 15 minCook 20 min

Cinnamon churros are a beloved traditional treat often enjoyed during the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe, celebrated on December 12th. These crispy, fried dough pastries coated in cinnamon sugar are a festive favorite in Mexican culture, symbolizing warmth and community during the holiday.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup water (240 ml)
  • 2 1/2 tablespoons granulated sugar (31 g)
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (30 ml)
  • 1 cup all-purpose flour (120 g)
  • 2 quarts vegetable oil for frying (1.9 L)
  • 1/2 cup granulated sugar (100 g)
  • 1 tablespoon ground cinnamon (8 g)

Method

  1. In a medium saucepan, combine water, 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, salt, and 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. Bring to a boil over medium heat.
  2. Remove from heat and stir in the flour all at once until the mixture forms a ball and pulls away from the sides of the pan.
  3. Let the dough cool for 5 minutes.
  4. Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or large heavy pot to 375°F (190°C).
  5. Transfer the dough to a pastry bag fitted with a large star tip.
  6. Carefully pipe 4- to 6-inch (10-15 cm) strips of dough into the hot oil, cutting with scissors or a knife to release them.
  7. Fry churros in batches until golden brown, about 2 to 3 minutes per side.
  8. Remove churros with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
  9. Combine 1/2 cup sugar and cinnamon in a shallow dish.
  10. Roll warm churros in the cinnamon sugar mixture until fully coated.
  11. Serve immediately, optionally with chocolate dipping sauce.

Tips

  • Use a large star-shaped piping tip for the classic ridged texture.
  • Keep the oil temperature steady to ensure churros cook evenly without absorbing excess oil.
  • Serve churros warm for the best texture and flavor.
